boundaries: MMOs are distinguished from other genres by their requirement for continuous online connectivity with persistent shared servers and large concurrent player populations, whereas action, RPG, and strategy games can be played solo or in small groups, and simulation, sports, and casual games do not inherently emphasize multiplayer world persistence.

name: Music and Party Video Games
display_name: Video Gaming: Music and Party Video Games
path: Video Gaming > Video Game Genres > Music and Party Video Games
description: Music-based games and party games are video games designed primarily around rhythm mechanics, musical performance, social multiplayer interaction, or competitive mini-games played with multiple players in a shared space.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by its focus on either rhythmic gameplay tied to music tracks or turn-based social competition, whereas Action games emphasize combat reflexes, Sports games simulate athletic competition, Party games emphasize social multiplayer fun, and Casual games encompass broader accessible experiences without these specific defining mechanics.

name: Puzzle Video Games
path: Video Gaming > Video Game Genres > Puzzle Video Games
description: Puzzle video games are games where the primary objective involves solving logic-based, pattern-matching, or spatial reasoning challenges that require player intelligence rather than reflexes or physical skill.
boundaries: Puzzle games are distinguished from action games by emphasizing cerebral challenge over timing and reaction speed, from strategy games by focusing on discrete puzzles rather than resource management or tactical decision-making, and from casual games by requiring systematic problem-solving rather than minimal engagement mechanics.

name: Content Channel
description: Content distributed through specific digital or physical platforms and mediums where audiences consume information and engage with brands.
boundaries: This category classifies where content is delivered (channels like social media, email, or marketplaces), whereas sibling categories like "Automotive" or "Food & Drink" classify what the content is about, and siblings like "Content Type" or "Content Media Format" classify how content is structured or formatted.

name: Editorial/Professional
description: Content published through established journalistic, professional publication, or credentialed expert platforms that prioritize editorial standards, fact-checking, and authoritative information delivery.
boundaries: This category differs from siblings by requiring editorial gatekeeping and professional credibility standards, whereas Social allows user-generated content, Email is a direct communication format, Search/Listings aggregates varied sources, and Marketplace/eCommerce prioritizes transactions over information authority.

name: Email
description: Email messages sent directly to users' inboxes by organizations, marketers, or individuals for communication, notifications, newsletters, or promotional purposes.
boundaries: Email is distinguished from its siblings by being asynchronous, point-to-point communication delivered to personal inbox accounts rather than public platforms, marketplaces, search results, community spaces, interactive games, standalone tools, or voice interfaces.

name: Forum/Community
description: Forum/Community content is published on platforms where users engage in threaded discussions, post questions, share experiences, and build communities around shared interests or topics.
boundaries: This category differs from siblings by requiring direct user-to-user interaction and persistent discussion threads, distinguishing it from Editorial's one-way publishing, Email's direct messaging, Social's brief posts, and Marketplace's transaction focus.

name: Game
description: Games and interactive entertainment experiences designed primarily for amusement, engagement, or competition, whether web-based, mobile, or embedded applications.
boundaries: Game content differs from Social platforms (which facilitate user connection), Utility/Online Tools (which solve functional problems), and Marketplace channels (which facilitate transactions) by being created and distributed fundamentally for play, entertainment, or competitive engagement rather than communication, productivity, or commerce.

name: Marketplace/eCommerce
description: Content intended for distribution and consumption through online platforms where goods, services, or digital products are bought, sold, or transacted directly by users.
boundaries: This category excludes editorial or professional content sites, asynchronous communication channels, community discussions, gaming platforms, search results, social networks, productivity tools, and voice-activated assistants—focusing specifically on platforms built around commercial transactions and shopping functionality.

name: Search Engine/Listings
description: Content delivered through search engine results pages, search engine marketing platforms, or business listing services where users discover information by querying or browsing categorized listings.
boundaries: This category differs from siblings by focusing on discovery mechanisms where users actively search for information or browse curated business directories, rather than consuming editorially-selected content, community discussions, social feeds, or transactional marketplaces.

name: Social
description: Social media platforms and networks where content is shared, discussed, and distributed through user profiles, feeds, posts, and direct messaging.
boundaries: Social differs from Editorial/Professional (formal publishing), Email (direct messaging), Forum/Community (discussion-focused sites), Marketplace/eCommerce (transactional), and Utility/Online Tools (functional) by emphasizing user-generated content, social graphs, and algorithmic feed distribution rather than professional curation, commerce transactions, or tool functionality.

name: Utility/Online Tool
description: An interactive digital platform or application that users access to accomplish a specific task, solve a problem, or perform a service without primarily seeking entertainment, social connection, or commercial transactions.
boundaries: This category encompasses self-service platforms that enable users to execute defined functions or obtain tools—distinguishing it from Editorial content (informational only), Social channels (connection-focused), Marketplace platforms (transaction-focused), Forums (discussion-focused), Games (entertainment-focused), Search/Listings (discovery-focused), Email (messaging-focused), and Voice channels (voice-interaction-focused).

name: Voice Activated Channels
description: Voice Activated Channels content is delivered through audio-based interfaces where users interact via spoken commands or questions to receive information, perform tasks, or control devices.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from siblings by its primary interaction method being voice input rather than text, visual, or written communication, making it unique among channels that rely on typing, reading, or traditional media consumption.

name: Content Type
description: Content that can be classified by its primary subject matter or topic domain, ranging from specialized fields like automotive and medical health to broad lifestyle categories like travel and entertainment.
boundaries: This category distinguishes itself from its siblings by organizing content based on **what topic or subject it addresses**, whereas Content Channel focuses on distribution platform, Content Source on origin, Content Media Format on presentation method, Content Language on linguistic encoding, and Content Source Geo on geographic location.

name: Academic/ResearchConent
description: Peer-reviewed articles, experimental data, methodological papers, and scholarly work that advances knowledge within academic disciplines and research fields.
boundaries: This category differs from Educational Content by focusing on original research contributions and novel findings rather than teaching existing knowledge, and differs from Instructional Content by emphasizing theoretical inquiry and evidence-based discovery over practical how-to guidance.

name: Chat/IM/Comments
description: Chat/IM/Comments content includes real-time or asynchronous conversational exchanges, direct messages, discussion threads, and user-generated comment sections across platforms like messaging apps, social media, forums, and comment threads.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from siblings by its focus on informal, dialogue-based user interactions rather than formal knowledge sharing (Academic/Research, Educational, Instructional), entertainment media (Entertainment), curated information (News), evaluations (Review), structured data (Listings/Search Results), or platform-specific features and social feeds (Feature, General Social, Interactive Content).

name: Educational Content
description: Content designed to teach, explain, or increase understanding of concepts, subjects, or skills through structured presentation of information.
boundaries: Educational Content differs from Academic/Research Content by focusing on learning and comprehension rather than original inquiry or scholarly contribution, and differs from Instructional Content by emphasizing conceptual understanding over step-by-step procedural guidance.

name: Entertainment Content
description: Entertainment Content is material created primarily to amuse, engage, or provide leisure enjoyment to audiences through narrative, humor, performance, or spectacle.
boundaries: This category excludes educational or instructional material designed to teach, news reporting focused on informing, reviews that critique products or services, and social conversation or comments that lack entertainment purpose, distinguishing it by prioritizing enjoyment over information delivery or knowledge transfer.

name: Feature
description: Content that introduces, explains, or highlights a specific capability, product update, or notable aspect of a service in a dedicated, substantial piece of writing or media.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by focusing on deep dives into particular offerings or updates rather than news reporting, educational instruction, academic rigor, user interaction, entertainment value, classified listings, reviews, or general social discussion.

name: General Social
description: General Social content includes posts, updates, and messages shared on social platforms where users engage in casual conversation, share personal moments, or discuss topics of general interest without a specific professional, educational, or entertainment focus.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by encompassing informal peer-to-peer communication and personal sharing, whereas Academic/Research focuses on scholarly work, Chat/IM/Comments captures direct messaging and threaded replies, Educational Content teaches specific skills, Entertainment provides leisure content, Features are curated articles, Instructional Content provides how-to guidance, Interactive Content requires active participation, Listings serve transactional purposes, News reports current events, and Reviews evaluate specific products or services.

name: Instructional Content
description: Content that teaches specific skills, procedures, or knowledge through step-by-step guidance, tutorials, how-to guides, or training materials designed for direct practical application.
boundaries: This category differs from Educational Content by focusing on actionable procedural learning rather than broad subject knowledge, and from Academic/Research Content by prioritizing practical application over theoretical analysis or original research findings.

name: Interactive Content
description: Interactive Content is material designed to actively engage users in participation, manipulation, or response, requiring user input or action to deliver value or reveal information.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by emphasizing user participation and bidirectional engagement, whereas Academic/Research Content prioritizes knowledge documentation, Educational Content focuses on structured learning, Instructional Content provides procedural guidance, News delivers information, and Entertainment Content offers passive enjoyment without requiring interaction for core value.

name: Listings/Classifieds/Product Listings/Search Results
description: This category contains structured compilations of items, services, or products presented in organized formats (such as search results, classified advertisements, marketplace listings, or product catalogs) where users browse, filter, and compare multiple options.
boundaries: It is distinguished from sibling categories by presenting aggregated, comparable items in standardized formats rather than original authored content (News, Feature), user discussions (Chat/IM/Comments, General Social), educational material (Educational Content, Instructional Content, Academic/Research Content), entertainment (Entertainment Content), evaluative analysis (Review), or interactive experiences (Interactive Content).

name: News
description: News consists of factual reporting about current events, recent developments, and timely information presented by journalistic sources or news organizations.
boundaries: News is distinguished from its siblings by its focus on reporting recent factual events rather than providing analysis (Feature), entertainment (Entertainment Content), education (Educational Content), user-generated discussion (Chat/IM/Comments), academic research (Academic/Research Content), reviews of products or services (Review), practical how-to guidance (Instructional Content), or catalog-style information (Listings/Classifieds/Product Listings/Search Results).

name: Review
description: A Review is evaluative content that assesses and provides opinions about specific products, services, experiences, media, or establishments based on personal experience or analysis.
boundaries: Review is distinguished from its siblings by its primary purpose of rendering judgment and recommendation on a particular subject, whereas News reports events, Entertainment provides amusement, Educational Content teaches concepts, Instructional Content teaches processes, and Academic/Research Content conducts scholarly investigation.

name: Content Source
description: This category classifies content based on its origin or the entity responsible for creating or publishing it.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by focusing on *who produced the content* rather than its subject matter (like Automotive or Food & Drink), its format (like Content Media Format), or where it appears (like Content Channel).

name: Professionally Produced
description: Content created by established media organizations, production companies, or professional creators with editorial oversight, production budgets, and quality control standards.
boundaries: This category differs from User Generated content by requiring professional creation infrastructure and editorial processes, and differs from Aggregated/Curated content by being original productions rather than collections of existing material from multiple sources.

name: User Generated
description: Content created directly by individual users, community members, or non-professional contributors sharing their own experiences, opinions, or creations.
boundaries: User Generated content originates from the audience themselves rather than being produced by professional creators or assembled from existing sources by curators.

name: Aggregated/Curated
description: This category contains content that has been collected, compiled, and organized from multiple sources by editors, algorithms, or platforms rather than originally created by the publishing entity.
boundaries: It differs from Professionally Produced content, which is created directly by the publishing organization, and from User Generated content, which originates from individual users and community members.

name: Content Media Format
display_name: Content Media Format: Content Media Format
description: Content that is organized and delivered in different technical formats such as audio, video, text, images, or interactive elements.
boundaries: This category classifies content based on its delivery medium and technical presentation, while sibling categories classify content by subject matter (Movies, Sports), distribution channel (Content Channel), creation type (Content Type), or other metadata dimensions (Content Language, Content Source Geo).

name: Audio
description: Audio content includes podcasts, music, sound effects, audiobooks, voice recordings, and other material primarily experienced through listening.
boundaries: Audio differs from Video by excluding visual components, from Textual by requiring auditory rather than written consumption, from Interactive by presenting linear playback without user-driven navigation, and from Images/Galleries, Mixed, and VR/AR by focusing solely on sound without visual or immersive elements.

name: Images/Galleries
description: This category encompasses static visual content presented as individual images, photo collections, slideshows, or organized gallery displays.
boundaries: It is distinguished from sibling categories by its reliance on non-moving visual representation, setting it apart from Video and VR/AR which incorporate motion or immersion, Audio which prioritizes sound, Interactive which requires user manipulation, Mixed which combines multiple formats equally, and Textual which centers on written language.

name: Interactive
description: Content that requires active user participation or manipulation to consume, such as quizzes, games, simulations, calculators, or dynamic tools where the user's input directly influences the experience.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by centering on user agency and responsiveness—while Audio, Images, Textual, and Video are consumed passively, and Mixed combines multiple passive formats, Interactive demands direct engagement to function or reveal its full value.

name: Mixed
description: Content that combines two or more distinct media types (such as text with images, audio with video, or text with interactive elements) into a single integrated presentation.
boundaries: Mixed content differs from single-format categories by requiring simultaneous use of multiple media modalities, whereas each sibling category contains content dominated by or exclusive to one primary media type.

name: Textual
description: Content that communicates primarily through written words, including articles, blog posts, essays, transcripts, and written documentation.
boundaries: Textual content relies exclusively on the written word for meaning, whereas Audio uses sound, Images/Galleries uses visual stills, Video uses moving visuals, Interactive requires user input, Mixed combines multiple formats equally, and VR/AR creates immersive spatial experiences.

name: Video
description: Video content is material presented as moving sequences of images with synchronized sound designed for visual and auditory consumption.
boundaries: Video is distinguished from Audio by its requirement for visual component, from Images/Galleries by its temporal dimension and motion, from Interactive by its passive viewing nature, from Mixed by being a single unified format rather than combined types, from Textual by using primarily visual narrative, and from VR/AR by existing in 2D fixed-perspective presentation.

name: VR/AR
description: Immersive digital experiences that use virtual reality or augmented reality technologies to overlay digital information onto physical environments or create fully simulated three-dimensional worlds for user interaction.
boundaries: This category differs from Interactive content by requiring specialized headsets or devices that fundamentally alter spatial perception, and from Mixed content by focusing specifically on VR/AR technologies rather than combining multiple standard media types.

name: Content Language
description: Content is presented or written in a specific human language that determines how audiences access and understand the material.
boundaries: This category differs from its siblings by classifying content based on the linguistic medium of communication rather than subject matter (like Business or Sports), distribution channel (like Content Channel), structural format (like Content Type), or geographic origin (like Content Source Geo).

name: Afar
description: Afar is a Cushitic language spoken primarily by the Afar people in the Horn of Africa, particularly in Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Djibouti.
boundaries: Afar is distinguished from its siblings by being a low-resource Cushitic language of the Horn of Africa region, whereas most siblings are either major languages with broader geographic distribution or belong to different language families entirely.

name: Abkhaz
description: Content coded in Abkhaz, a Northwest Caucasian language primarily spoken in the Republic of Abkhazia and the diaspora.
boundaries: Abkhaz is distinguished from its sibling categories by its classification as a Caucasian language with a unique phonological inventory, separate from the Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Austronesian, Sino-Tibetan, and other major language families represented among the siblings.

name: Avestan
description: Avestan is an ancient Eastern Iranian language in which the Zoroastrian sacred texts, the Avesta, were composed and preserved.
boundaries: Avestan is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an extinct ancient language rather than a modern spoken or literary language, and by its specific association with Zoroastrianism and pre-Islamic Persian religious traditions.

name: Afrikaans
description: Afrikaans is a West Germanic language that evolved from Dutch dialects spoken in South Africa and Namibia, characterized by simplified grammar and vocabulary influenced by indigenous African languages and other European languages.
boundaries: Afrikaans is distinguished from other Germanic languages (like Dutch, German, and English) by its origin in Southern Africa and its unique phonological and grammatical simplifications, and from other African languages by its Indo-European roots and structural classification as a Germanic tongue.

name: Akan
description: Akan is a Kwa language spoken primarily in Ghana by the Akan people, including major dialect groups such as Twi and Fante.
boundaries: Akan is distinguished from its siblings as the only Kwa language from West Africa in this taxonomy, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Niger-Congo languages from other regions, or constructed languages.

name: Amharic
description: Amharic is a Semitic language spoken primarily in Ethiopia, written in the Ge'ez script, and serves as the official language of the Ethiopian state.
boundaries: Amharic is distinguished from other languages in this taxonomy by its classification as an Ethio-Semitic language with unique phonological and grammatical features, setting it apart from Indo-European languages, Sino-Tibetan languages, Niger-Congo languages, and other language families represented in the sibling categories.

name: Aragonese
description: Content written or transmitted in the Aragonese language, a Romance language spoken primarily in the Aragón region of northeastern Spain.
boundaries: Aragonese is distinguished from other Romance languages (such as Catalan, Spanish, Occitan, and Galician) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, and from other languages overall by being the native language of the Aragonese people rather than speakers of the sibling languages listed.

name: Arabic
description: Arabic is a Semitic language spoken primarily across the Middle East and North Africa, with multiple regional dialects and a standardized written form (Modern Standard Arabic).
boundaries: Arabic is distinguished from its sibling categories by its origin in the Semitic language family and its geographic concentration in the Arab world, whereas siblings represent diverse language families distributed across different global regions.

name: Assamese
description: Content that is written in or primarily associated with the Assamese language, a Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Assam region of northeastern India.
boundaries: Assamese is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the specific language of Assam and its speakers, rather than other languages from Africa, Europe, Asia, or other regions represented in the sibling list.

name: Avaric
description: Avaric is a Northeast Caucasian language spoken primarily by the Avar people in the Dagestan region of Russia.
boundaries: Avaric is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a non-Indo-European, agglutinative language from the Caucasus region, whereas most siblings are Indo-European languages or belong to other major language families.

name: Aymara
description: Aymara is an indigenous language spoken primarily in the Andes region of Bolivia, Peru, and Chile, with approximately one million native speakers.
boundaries: Aymara is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Native American language of the Aymaran language family, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, Austronesian, or Sino-Tibetan languages.

name: Azerbaijani
description: Azerbaijani is a Turkic language spoken primarily in Azerbaijan and parts of Iran, Turkey, and Russia, with approximately 30 million native speakers.
boundaries: Azerbaijani is distinguished from its siblings by being a northwestern Turkic language written in the Latin script (modern standard) or Cyrillic, whereas most sibling categories represent either unrelated language families (Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, etc.) or other Turkic languages like Turkish, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Turkmen, and Uyghur that differ in geographic origin and linguistic features.

name: Bashkir
description: Bashkir is a Turkic language spoken primarily by the Bashkir people in the Republic of Bashkortostan in Russia.
boundaries: Bashkir is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Turkic language from the Volga-Ural region, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Afro-Asiatic languages, or Turkic languages from Central Asia or the Caucasus.

name: Belarusian
description: This category contains content that is written, spoken, or otherwise expressed in Belarusian, the East Slavic language spoken primarily in Belarus.
boundaries: Belarusian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being specifically the language of Belarus, separate from closely related Slavic languages like Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, and Bulgarian, and from all other world languages in the list.

name: Bulgarian
description: Bulgarian is a South Slavic language spoken primarily in Bulgaria and by diaspora communities, characterized by its loss of grammatical case, use of the definite article suffix, and three-way aspectual system.
boundaries: Bulgarian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole representative of the South Slavic branch among languages that include other Slavic groups (East Slavic like Russian and Ukrainian, West Slavic like Polish and Czech) and non-Slavic language families.

name: Bihari
description: Content in the Bihari language, a language of Indo-Aryan origin spoken primarily in the Bihar region of India and parts of Nepal.
boundaries: Bihari is distinguished from its siblings as a specific Indo-Aryan language of eastern India, separate from related languages like Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, and Assamese that occupy different geographic and linguistic spaces.

name: Bislama
description: Bislama is an English-based creole language spoken primarily in Vanuatu, developed from pidgin English used in colonial trade and labor contexts.
boundaries: Bislama is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a creole language with English as its lexical base and simplified grammar, rather than a natural language that evolved organically within a speech community or an artificial/constructed language.

name: Bambara
description: Bambara is a Niger-Congo language spoken primarily in Mali and used as a lingua franca across West Africa.
boundaries: Bambara differs from its siblings as a Mandinka language of the Mande language family, whereas siblings represent languages from other families, unrelated language groups, or geographic regions outside Mali and the broader Mande sphere.

name: Bengali
description: Content in this category is written in Bengali, an Indo-Aryan language primarily spoken in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.
boundaries: Bengali is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic classification as an Indo-Aryan language with its own script system, grammar, and vocabulary, rather than being any of the other 200+ languages represented among the sibling categories.

name: Tibetan
description: Content written in Tibetan, a Sino-Tibetan language primarily spoken in the Tibetan plateau region of Asia.
boundaries: Tibetan is distinguished from its sibling categories by its unique script system, grammatical structure, and geographic association with the Tibetan cultural region, rather than by proximity to other Asian or European language families.

name: Breton
description: Content in the Breton language, which is a Brythonic Celtic language spoken primarily in Brittany, France.
boundaries: Breton is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a minority Celtic language of northwestern France, whereas siblings include major European languages, languages from other language families (Afro-Asiatic, Indo-Aryan, Sino-Tibetan, etc.), and other Celtic languages like Welsh, Irish, and Scottish Gaelic.

name: Bosnian
description: Bosnian is a South Slavic language spoken primarily in Bosnia and Herzegovina, characterized by its use of the Latin alphabet and its position within the Serbo-Croatian language continuum.
boundaries: Bosnian is distinguished from other Slavic languages (such as Serbian, Croatian, and Montenegrin) by its specific standardization, vocabulary choices, and status as an official language of Bosnia and Herzegovina, while differing from non-Slavic languages through its Slavic grammatical structure and linguistic features.

name: Catalan
description: Content primarily created in or translated into Catalan, a Romance language spoken in Catalonia, Valencia, the Balearic Islands, and other regions in northeastern Spain and southern France.
boundaries: Catalan is distinguished from other Romance languages in its sibling categories (such as Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, and Galician) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, and from non-Romance languages by its linguistic family classification.

name: Chechen
description: Content in Chechen language consists of text, audio, video, or other media where Chechen, a Northeast Caucasian language spoken primarily in the Chechen Republic, is the primary language of expression.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by identifying Chechen as the specific language used, whereas sibling categories each represent their own distinct natural or constructed language from the global linguistic inventory.

name: Chamorro
description: Content in this category consists of works, documents, or media primarily composed in Chamorro, the Austronesian language native to the Mariana Islands and spoken by Chamorro people.
boundaries: Chamorro is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole representative of the Mariana Islands language group, while siblings represent other distinct languages from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Pacific, and the Americas.

name: Corsican
description: Content that is written in Corsican, a Romance language spoken primarily in Corsica and diaspora communities.
boundaries: Corsican is distinguished from its sibling languages by being the specific Romance language of Corsica, separate from French, Italian, Sardinian, and other Romance languages in the taxonomy.

name: Cree
description: Content primarily created in or translated into Cree, an Algonquian language spoken by Indigenous peoples in Canada.
boundaries: Cree is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific North American Indigenous language, separate from the European, African, Asian, and other world languages represented in the sibling set.

name: Czech
description: Content that is written, spoken, or otherwise expressed in the Czech language, a West Slavic language primarily used in the Czech Republic.
boundaries: Czech is distinguished from other sibling language categories by its specific linguistic characteristics as a West Slavic language, including its grammar, phonetics, and vocabulary, rather than being grouped with Romance, Germanic, Indo-Aryan, or other language families represented among the siblings.

name: Old Church Slavonic
description: Old Church Slavonic is an ancient liturgical language that served as the literary and ecclesiastical standard for medieval Slavic peoples, particularly in Orthodox Christian contexts from the 9th century onward.
boundaries: Old Church Slavonic is distinguished from its siblings as a historical, primarily liturgical language no longer spoken natively, whereas most siblings are either modern living languages or historically attested languages with contemporary speaker communities.

name: Chuvash
description: Chuvash is a Turkic language spoken primarily in the Chuvash Republic of Russia and by diaspora communities, characterized by unique phonological features including palatalization and vowel harmony distinct from other Turkic languages.
boundaries: Chuvash is distinguished from other Turkic languages (Azerbaijani, Bashkir, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Turkmen, Tatar, Turkish, Uyghur, Uzbek) by its specific sound system and grammatical structure, and from all non-Turkic sibling categories by its membership in the Turkic language family.

name: Welsh
description: Welsh is a Celtic language spoken primarily in Wales, characterized by its distinctive phonology, grammar, and vocabulary rooted in the Brythonic branch of Celtic languages.
boundaries: Welsh is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole representative of the Welsh language, whereas siblings represent other individual languages from diverse linguistic families across the world.

name: Danish
description: Danish is a North Germanic language primarily spoken in Denmark and parts of Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
boundaries: Danish is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of Denmark, while other Germanic siblings like German, Swedish, Norwegian, and Faroese are associated with different Scandinavian and Germanic-speaking regions.

name: German
description: German is a West Germanic language primarily spoken in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and neighboring regions, characterized by its grammatical cases, gender-inflected nouns, and complex verb conjugation systems.
boundaries: German is distinguished from other European languages by its specific phonological features, grammatical structure (including four cases and three genders), and its classification within the West Germanic branch rather than Romance, Slavic, or other language families represented in the sibling categories.

name: Divehi
description: Divehi is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the Maldives and by diaspora communities, written in the Thaana script.
boundaries: Divehi is distinguished from its siblings by being the official language of the Maldives and the only Indo-Aryan language in this set that uses the Thaana script rather than Latin, Devanagari, or other scripts common to related languages.

name: Dzongkha
description: Dzongkha is the official language of Bhutan, a Sino-Tibetan language spoken primarily in the Bhutanese Himalayan region with its own unique script and linguistic features.
boundaries: Dzongkha is distinguished from its siblings by being the sole representative of Bhutanese language content, whereas sibling categories each represent other individual languages from diverse linguistic families and geographic regions worldwide.

name: Ewe
description: Content in the Ewe language, a Niger-Congo language spoken primarily in Ghana and Togo by the Ewe people.
boundaries: Ewe is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Kwa language of West Africa, rather than belonging to other language families such as Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Altaic, Dravidian, Sino-Tibetan, or other Niger-Congo branches.

name: Greek
description: Content in the Greek language, including both Ancient Greek (Classical and Hellenistic periods) and Modern Greek as used in Greece, Cyprus, and Greek diaspora communities.
boundaries: Greek is distinguished from other language categories by its unique alphabetic script, its Indo-European linguistic structure with distinct grammatical features, and its historical continuity spanning over 3,400 years while maintaining a recognizable linguistic identity separate from Romance, Germanic, Slavic, and other major language families represented in the sibling categories.

name: English
description: Content that is written, spoken, or primarily presented in the English language, encompassing all varieties and dialects including British, American, Australian, and other regional forms.
boundaries: English is distinguished from all other language categories by its specific linguistic system, grammar, vocabulary, and phonetic characteristics, rather than by geographical origin or historical period.

name: Esperanto
description: Esperanto is an artificially constructed international auxiliary language created in 1887 by L.L. Zamenhof, designed to promote peace and understanding by providing a neutral means of communication between speakers of different natural languages.
boundaries: Esperanto is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a planned/constructed language rather than a natural language that evolved organically within a speech community, and by its explicit purpose as an international auxiliary language rather than the primary language of any nation or ethnic group.

name: Spanish
description: Spanish is content primarily written or spoken in the Spanish language, a Romance language with approximately 500 million native speakers originating from the Iberian Peninsula and widely spoken across Latin America and other regions.
boundaries: Spanish is distinguished from other Romance languages (French, Italian, Portuguese, Romansh, Romanian, Galician, Catalan, Occitan) and all non-Romance language categories by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, including its characteristic use of the theta sound, subjunctive mood constructions, and distinctive vocabulary.

name: Estonian
description: Content in this category is written in Estonian, a Finno-Ugric language spoken primarily in Estonia and characterized by its agglutinative grammar and vowel harmony.
boundaries: Estonian is distinguished from its siblings as the official language of Estonia and the only Finno-Ugric language in this taxonomy besides Finnish, Hungarian, and a few others, making it unique among the predominantly Indo-European languages in this classification.

name: Basque
description: Content written in or primarily spoken as Basque, an agglutinative language spoken in the Basque Country region of northern Spain and southwestern France.
boundaries: Basque is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the only non-Indo-European language in this list, making it a language isolate unrelated to the Romance, Germanic, Slavic, or other language families represented by the other categories.

name: Farsi
description: Content created, produced, or primarily presented in Farsi (also known as Persian), an Indo-European language spoken primarily in Iran, Afghanistan, and Tajikistan.
boundaries: Farsi is distinguished from its sibling categories by its classification as a southwestern Iranian language using the Persian script, whereas siblings encompass all other world languages including other Iranian languages (Kurdish, Tajik, Pashto), neighboring languages (Arabic, Turkish, Urdu), and unrelated language families.

name: Fula
description: Fula is a Niger-Congo language spoken primarily across West Africa by the Fulani people, with significant populations in Senegal, Guinea, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Nigeria.
boundaries: Fula is distinguished from other African languages in this list by being a specifically Atlantic-Congo language of the Senegambian region, rather than being a Semitic language (like Arabic or Amharic), a Bantu language (like Swahili or Zulu), or an Afro-Asiatic language from the Horn of Africa (like Oromo or Tigrinya).

name: Finnish
description: Finnish is content written in the Finnish language, a Uralic language spoken primarily in Finland and characterized by its unique grammatical structure including extensive case systems and vowel harmony.
boundaries: Finnish is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of Finland, whereas the siblings represent other distinct natural languages from different language families (Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, etc.) or artificial constructed languages.

name: Fijian
description: Fijian is an Austronesian language spoken primarily in Fiji, characterized by Melanesian linguistic features and used as both an official and community language in the South Pacific island nation.
boundaries: Fijian is distinguished from other languages in this category by being a Pacific Islander language specific to Fiji, whereas its siblings represent diverse language families and geographic regions spanning from African languages like Swahili and Yoruba to European languages like French and German to Asian languages like Japanese and Hindi.

name: Faroese
description: Content in the Faroese language, which is a North Germanic language spoken primarily in the Faroe Islands and by diaspora communities.
boundaries: Faroese is distinguished from other Germanic languages by being a North Germanic language most closely related to Icelandic and Old Norse, whereas its siblings include other Germanic branches (West Germanic like German, Dutch, English; North Germanic like Icelandic; and other language families entirely).

name: French
description: This category contains content that is written in or primarily presented in the French language, including modern standard French and its recognized variants.
boundaries: French is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as a Romance language primarily spoken in France and other Francophone regions, rather than any of the other individual world languages represented as siblings.

name: Western Frisian
description: Western Frisian is a North Sea Germanic language spoken primarily in the province of Friesland in the Netherlands.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from other Germanic languages by its specific geographic origin in the Frisian region and its linguistic features that place it between English and Dutch rather than being a dialect of either.

name: Irish
description: Content that is written, spoken, or produced in Irish (Gaeilge), the Celtic language primarily used in Ireland.
boundaries: Irish is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of the Republic of Ireland and a Celtic language, whereas siblings include Romance languages (French, Spanish, Italian), Germanic languages (English, German, Dutch), Slavic languages (Russian, Polish, Czech), and many other language families from across the world.

name: Scottish Gaelic
description: Content tagged with this category is primarily written in or spoken as Scottish Gaelic, a Goidelic language native to the Scottish Highlands and Islands.
boundaries: Scottish Gaelic is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the Celtic language of Scotland, separate from Irish Gaelic, Welsh, Breton, and Cornish, and from all other non-Celtic languages in this taxonomy.

name: Galician
description: Content that is written, spoken, or otherwise expressed in Galician, the Romance language spoken primarily in Galicia in northwestern Spain.
boundaries: Galician is distinguished from other Romance languages (such as Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan, and Occitan) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, and from other language categories by being explicitly designated as Galician rather than a related or neighboring language.

name: Guarani
description: Content that is primarily written or spoken in Guarani, an indigenous language of South America spoken mainly in Paraguay, Argentina, and Brazil.
boundaries: Guarani is distinguished from its sibling categories as the sole representative of the Tupian language family, whereas siblings represent languages from Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, Austronesian, Dravidian, and other major language families.

name: Gujarati
description: Gujarati is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the Gujarat state of India and by diaspora communities worldwide, characterized by its own distinct script and grammatical structure.
boundaries: Gujarati is distinguished from its sibling categories by being specifically the language of Gujarat and its speakers, rather than any of the other individual natural languages or constructed languages in the broader Content Language taxonomy.

name: Manx
description: Content expressed in Manx, a Goidelic language historically spoken on the Isle of Man.
boundaries: Manx is distinguished from other language categories by being a Celtic language specific to the Isle of Man, separate from Irish, Scottish Gaelic, Welsh, Breton, and Cornish which represent other Celtic language traditions.

name: Hausa
description: Hausa is a Chadic language spoken primarily in Niger and Nigeria by millions of native speakers as a lingua franca across West Africa.
boundaries: Hausa is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the only Chadic language in this taxonomy, whereas its siblings represent other language families such as Niger-Congo, Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, and Sino-Tibetan languages.

name: Hebrew
description: Content in Hebrew language includes text, audio, video, and other media whose primary language is Hebrew, whether ancient, medieval, or modern standard Hebrew.
boundaries: Hebrew is distinguished from other Semitic languages (Arabic, Amharic, Tigrinya) and other language categories by being the official language of Israel and the liturgical language of Judaism, with its own distinct writing system and linguistic characteristics.

name: Hindi
description: Hindi is a language primarily spoken in India, belonging to the Indo-Aryan language family, and characterized as the official language of the Indian Union and a lingua franca across much of North India.
boundaries: Hindi is distinguished from other Indo-Aryan languages in this taxonomy (such as Bengali, Punjabi, Marathi, Gujarati, and Urdu) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, as well as its geographic and cultural association with the Hindi heartland of central and northern India.

name: Hiri Motu
description: Hiri Motu is an Austronesian language spoken in Papua New Guinea, primarily used as a lingua franca in the central regions of the country.
boundaries: Hiri Motu is distinguished from its siblings by being a Papuan language with Austronesian roots, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Sino-Tibetan languages, or other major language families from Africa, Asia, and Europe.

name: Croatian
description: Croatian is a South Slavic language spoken primarily in Croatia, characterized by its use of the Latin alphabet and distinctive phonological and grammatical features including three genders and seven cases.
boundaries: Croatian is distinguished from other Slavic languages (Bulgarian, Belarusian, Czech, Slovak, Slovene, Serbian, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish) by its specific phonemic inventory, accentuation system, and lexical features, and from non-Slavic siblings by its membership in the South Slavic branch.

name: Haitian
description: Content written in Haitian Creole, a French-based creole language spoken primarily in Haiti and its diaspora communities.
boundaries: Haitian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a creole language derived from French and African languages, rather than a standard national or ethnic language.

name: Hungarian
description: Content that is written, spoken, or produced in the Hungarian language, a Finno-Ugric language spoken primarily in Hungary and surrounding regions.
boundaries: Hungarian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole Finno-Ugric language in this taxonomy, whereas most siblings are Indo-European languages or represent other distinct language families.

name: Armenian
description: Content written in Armenian, the Indo-European language primarily spoken in Armenia and by Armenian diaspora communities worldwide.
boundaries: Armenian is distinguished from its sibling categories by its unique Indo-European language family classification and its use of the distinctive Armenian alphabet, separating it from the vast majority of sibling languages that belong to other language families or use different writing systems.

name: Herero
description: Content in the Herero language, a Bantu language spoken primarily in Namibia and Botswana by the Herero people.
boundaries: Herero is distinguished from its siblings as a Bantu language of southern Africa, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Afro-Asiatic languages, or other language families with different geographic distributions and linguistic structures.

name: Interlingua
description: Interlingua is a constructed auxiliary language designed for international communication, created in 1951 by the International Auxiliary Language Association based on Romance language vocabulary and simplified grammar.
boundaries: Interlingua is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a deliberately engineered interlanguage rather than a naturally evolved language with native speakers or distinct ethnic/regional origins.

name: Indonesian
description: Content in Indonesian language comprises written or spoken material produced in Bahasa Indonesia, the official language of Indonesia and a lingua franca across the Indonesian archipelago.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by identifying content specifically in Indonesian rather than other world languages, including other Austronesian languages like Javanese, Sundanese, Tagalog, or Malay.

name: Interlingue
description: Interlingue is an artificial auxiliary language created in 1922 designed to be a simplified, easy-to-learn international language based primarily on Romance and Germanic language elements.
boundaries: Interlingue is distinguished from natural human languages and other constructed languages like Esperanto, Ido, and Volapük by its specific design principles emphasizing maximum intelligibility through systematic use of international vocabulary and regular grammatical patterns derived from major European languages.

name: Igbo
description: Content that is written in or primarily uses the Igbo language, a Niger-Congo language spoken by the Igbo people of southeastern Nigeria.
boundaries: Igbo is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific language of the Niger-Congo family from West Africa, rather than languages from other regions or language families represented in the siblings.

name: Nuosu
description: Nuosu is a Sino-Tibetan language spoken primarily by the Yi people in the Liangshan region of southwestern China.
boundaries: Nuosu is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the standardized literary form of the Yi language, whereas its siblings represent distinct natural languages from other language families and regions worldwide.

name: Inupiaq
description: Inupiaq is an Eskimo-Aleut language spoken by indigenous Inupiat peoples in northern Alaska and northwestern Canada.
boundaries: Inupiaq is distinguished from its siblings as a polysynthetic indigenous language of the Arctic region, separate from other Native American languages like Navajo, Cree, and Ojibwe by its linguistic family and distinct from other Inuit languages like Inuktitut and Kalaallisut by its specific regional dialect and speaker community.

name: Ido
description: Ido is an artificial international auxiliary language created in 1907 as a reform of Esperanto, designed to be a neutral means of communication between speakers of different native languages.
boundaries: Ido differs from its sibling categories by being a constructed language intentionally engineered for international communication, whereas sibling categories represent natural languages that evolved organically within specific speech communities.

name: Icelandic
description: Content in this category is authored, published, or primarily presented in Icelandic, the official language of Iceland and a North Germanic language spoken by approximately 350,000 native speakers.
boundaries: Icelandic is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole Nordic language in this list that preserved Old Norse grammatical structures and maintained relatively conservative phonological features, setting it apart from related languages like Faroese, Danish, Swedish, and Norwegian.

name: Italian
description: Italian is a Romance language spoken primarily in Italy and among diaspora communities worldwide, used for content creation, communication, and documentation in Italian-speaking regions.
boundaries: Italian is distinguished from other Romance languages (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Romanian) and non-Romance sibling categories by its specific linguistic features, geographic origin in the Italian peninsula, and distinct phonological and grammatical characteristics.

name: Inuktitut
description: Content in Inuktitut language, the official language of Nunavut and a co-official language in the Northwest Territories and Nunatsiavut, consisting of multiple dialects spoken by Inuit peoples in the Canadian Arctic.
boundaries: Inuktitut is distinguished from its sibling categories as the only Eskimo-Aleut language in this taxonomy, whereas all other siblings belong to language families spanning Africa, Asia, Europe, and other regions.

name: Japanese
description: Japanese is the official language of Japan and a major East Asian language with over 125 million native speakers, characterized by a writing system combining hiragana, katakana, and kanji characters.
boundaries: Japanese is distinguished from other Asian language siblings (such as Chinese, Korean, Thai, and Vietnamese) by its unique three-part writing system and grammatical structure, and from all other siblings by being the primary language of Japan rather than any other nation or region.

name: Javanese
description: Content that is written in Javanese, the Austronesian language spoken primarily in Java, Indonesia.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by identifying content specifically in the Javanese language rather than any other of the world's natural or constructed languages listed.

name: Georgian
description: Georgian is a South Caucasian language spoken primarily in the country of Georgia, with its own unique alphabet and grammatical structure.
boundaries: Georgian is distinguished from its siblings by being the sole representative of the South Caucasian language family, whereas siblings represent languages from Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, Austronesian, Sino-Tibetan, Dravidian, and other language families.

name: Kongo
description: Content in the Kongo language, a Bantu language spoken by the Kongo people primarily in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, and Angola.
boundaries: Kongo is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Bantu language of Central Africa, separate from other African languages like Swahili, Yoruba, and Hausa, and from all non-African languages in the sibling list.

name: Kikuyu
description: Kikuyu is a Bantu language spoken primarily by the Kikuyu people in the central highlands of Kenya.
boundaries: Kikuyu is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Bantu language of East Africa, whereas siblings include languages from diverse language families (Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, etc.) and geographic regions across the globe.

name: Kwanyama
description: Kwanyama is a Bantu language spoken primarily by the Kwanyama people in northern Namibia and southern Angola.
boundaries: Kwanyama is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Bantu language of southwestern Africa, whereas siblings represent either distinct language families (Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, etc.), other Bantu languages, or constructed/classical languages from different regions.

name: Kazakh
description: Content that is primarily written, spoken, or produced in Kazakh, the official language of Kazakhstan and a Turkic language spoken across Central Asia.
boundaries: Kazakh is distinguished from its siblings as a Turkic language primarily associated with Kazakhstan, whereas related Turkic languages like Azerbaijani, Kyrgyz, Turkish, Turkmen, and Uzbek are associated with different geographic regions and have distinct standardized forms.

name: Kalaallisut
description: Kalaallisut is the official language of Greenland, an Eskimo-Aleut language spoken primarily in the Arctic regions of Greenland and used in government, education, and daily life.
boundaries: Kalaallisut is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Greenlandic Inuit language from the Arctic, whereas its siblings represent languages from diverse geographic regions and language families including African, European, Asian, and indigenous languages from around the world.

name: Khmer
description: Khmer is the official language of Cambodia, spoken as a first language by approximately 16 million people and written in the Khmer script, a Southeast Asian abugida system.
boundaries: Khmer is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole Austroasiatic language in this language taxonomy, whereas siblings represent various Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, and other language families.

name: Kannada
description: Content tagged with Kannada language is material written in or primarily expressed through Kannada, a Dravidian language spoken in the Indian state of Karnataka.
boundaries: Kannada is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a South Indian Dravidian language, whereas most siblings are Indo-European languages (like Hindi, Bengali, or Sanskrit), Sino-Tibetan languages (like Chinese or Tibetan), Austronesian languages (like Javanese or Tagalog), or other language families entirely.

name: Korean
description: Content in the Korean language, including text, documents, media, and other materials written or produced in Korean.
boundaries: Korean is distinguished from its sibling categories as the language spoken primarily in North and South Korea, using the Hangul writing system, and is classified as a language isolate unrelated to Chinese, Japanese, or other East Asian language families represented among the siblings.

name: Kanuri
description: Kanuri is a Saharan language spoken primarily in Niger, Nigeria, and Chad by the Kanuri people and their descendants.
boundaries: Kanuri is distinguished from its siblings by being a Saharan language of Central Africa, whereas most siblings are either major European languages, widely-spoken Asian languages, or languages from other African language families like Niger-Congo or Afro-Asiatic.

name: Kashmiri
description: Kashmiri is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the Kashmir Valley region of South Asia, serving as the native language of the Kashmiri people.
boundaries: Kashmiri is distinguished from its siblings by being the specific language of the Kashmir region, rather than the broader languages of the Indian subcontinent (Hindi, Bengali, Urdu, Punjab, etc.) or other Indo-Aryan languages, and it occupies a unique linguistic position between Indic and Persian influences.

name: Kurdish
description: Kurdish is a Northwestern Iranian language spoken primarily by Kurdish populations across the Middle East, with multiple dialects and written standards.
boundaries: Kurdish is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific language from the Iranian branch of Indo-European languages, whereas its siblings represent distinct languages from various other language families and branches including Semitic, Turkic, Sino-Tibetan, Dravidian, and other language groups.

name: Komi
description: Content that is written or expressed in Komi, a Uralic language spoken primarily in the Komi Republic and surrounding regions of northwestern Russia.
boundaries: Komi is distinguished from its sibling language categories by its classification as a Uralic language native to the Russian Arctic, rather than Indo-European languages like Russian or neighboring Slavic tongues, or other language families represented in this taxonomy.

name: Cornish
description: Content in this category is written in Cornish, a Celtic language historically spoken in Cornwall, England, and currently experiencing a revival as a minority and revitalized language.
boundaries: Cornish is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the specific Celtic language of Cornwall, whereas other siblings represent either different language families (Germanic, Romance, Slavic, etc.), other Celtic languages (Welsh, Breton, Irish, Scottish Gaelic), or unrelated language groups.

name: Kyrgyz
description: Kyrgyz is a Turkic language spoken primarily in Kyrgyzstan and by diaspora communities across Central Asia and beyond.
boundaries: Kyrgyz is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the primary official language of Kyrgyzstan, whereas siblings represent the national or regional languages of other distinct territories and linguistic communities.

name: Latin
description: Content in this category is written in Latin, the ancient Italic language spoken in the Roman Empire and used as a scholarly and ecclesiastical lingua franca throughout medieval and early modern Europe.
boundaries: Latin is distinguished from its sibling categories as a dead classical language with no native speakers, whereas most siblings are modern spoken languages, and from Old Church Slavonic, Sanskrit, and Pali as Latin's primary domain was the Western Roman world rather than religious or South Asian contexts.

name: Luxembourgish
description: Content written or produced in Luxembourgish, the official language of Luxembourg and a Moselle Franconian dialect spoken primarily in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
boundaries: Luxembourgish is distinguished from other Germanic languages (like German, Dutch, and Afrikaans) by its status as the national language of Luxembourg and its specific phonological and lexical features of the Moselle Franconian linguistic group.

name: Ganda
description: Content in Ganda language comprises written, spoken, or multimedia materials produced in Ganda, the principal language of the Baganda people of Uganda with approximately 4 million native speakers.
boundaries: Ganda is distinguished from its siblings as a Bantu language of East-Central Africa, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Sino-Tibetan languages, Afro-Asiatic languages, or other language families from different geographic regions.

name: Limburgish
description: Limburgish is a Low Franconian language spoken in the Limburg region of the Netherlands, Belgium, and Germany, characterized by its own distinct phonological and grammatical features within the broader Germanic language family.
boundaries: Limburgish is distinguished from other sibling categories by being a regional Low Franconian language of Western Europe, whereas siblings include other unrelated language families (such as Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, or Sino-Tibetan) and distinct Romance, Celtic, Slavic, and other Germanic languages not classified as Low Franconian.

name: Lingala
description: Lingala is a Bantu language spoken primarily in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of the Congo, used as a lingua franca in trade, media, and daily communication across the region.
boundaries: Lingala is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a C30 Bantu language of Central Africa, whereas siblings include unrelated language families from Europe (Romance, Germanic, Slavic), Asia (Sino-Tibetan, Indo-European, Dravidian), and other African regions (Semitic, Cushitic, Nilotic).

name: Lao
description: Content that is written in or primarily uses the Lao language, a Tai-Kadai language spoken in Laos and northeastern Thailand.
boundaries: Lao is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as a tonal language of Southeast Asia, separate from other Tai languages like Thai and other regional languages in the taxonomy.

name: Lithuanian
description: Lithuanian is a Baltic language spoken primarily in Lithuania, belonging to the Indo-European language family and characterized by its conservative grammatical structure and distinctive phonological features.
boundaries: Lithuanian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole representative of the Baltic language branch, whereas siblings include other Indo-European families (Romance, Germanic, Slavic, Celtic, Greek, Italic), Uralic languages (Finnish, Hungarian, Estonian), and languages from entirely different families (Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, Dravidian, Altaic, Austronesian, and others).

name: Luba-Katanga
description: Luba-Katanga is a Bantu language spoken primarily in the Katanga region of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
boundaries: This category represents a specific regional Bantu language distinct from other African languages like Swahili, Kongo, Lingala, and Shona, which have different geographic distributions and linguistic characteristics.

name: Latvian
description: This category contains content that is written in or primarily presented in Latvian, the official language of Latvia.
boundaries: Latvian is distinguished from its sibling categories as a Baltic language spoken in Latvia, rather than being a language from other language families such as Slavic (Russian, Polish, Ukrainian), Romance (French, Spanish, Italian), Germanic (German, English, Swedish), or other language groups represented among the siblings.

name: Malagasy
description: Malagasy is an Austronesian language spoken primarily in Madagascar and by diaspora communities, characterized by grammatical features including verb-initial word order and extensive use of affixes.
boundaries: Malagasy is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole Austronesian language in this collection, while all other siblings represent languages from African, European, Asian, and other language families.

name: Marshallese
description: Content in this category is written in or represents the Marshallese language, the Austronesian language spoken in the Marshall Islands.
boundaries: Marshallese is distinguished from its siblings by being the primary language of the Marshall Islands, while other siblings represent distinct languages from different language families and geographic regions worldwide.

name: Māori
description: Content in Māori language, including texts, documents, audio, video, and other media produced in or translated into the Polynesian language spoken primarily in New Zealand.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by representing Māori, the indigenous Austronesian language of New Zealand, rather than any of the other world languages listed as sibling categories.

name: Macedonian
description: Content written or spoken in Macedonian, a South Slavic language primarily spoken in North Macedonia and diaspora communities.
boundaries: Macedonian is distinguished from other Slavic languages (Bulgarian, Serbian, Croatian, Slovene, Slovak, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, Belarusian, Czech) by its specific phonological, morphological, and lexical features, and from other South Slavic languages by its unique grammar and vocabulary.

name: Malayalam
description: Malayalam is a Dravidian language spoken primarily in Kerala, India, and is written in its own distinct script.
boundaries: Malayalam is distinguished from its siblings by being a South Indian Dravidian language with its unique script and grammatical structure, separate from the Indo-European languages (like Hindi, Tamil, Telugu) and other language families represented among the siblings.

name: Mongolian
description: Mongolian is a Mongolic language spoken primarily in Mongolia and by Mongolic peoples across Central and East Asia, featuring agglutinative grammar and traditionally written in the Mongolian script or Cyrillic.
boundaries: Mongolian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a language of the Mongolic language family, whereas the siblings represent languages from other language families such as Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, Sino-Tibetan, Austronesian, and others.

name: Marathi
description: Content that is written, published, or produced in the Marathi language, a major Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in Maharashtra state in India.
boundaries: Marathi is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as an Indo-Aryan language of western India, separate from other Indian languages like Hindi, Gujarati, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Urdu, Punjabi, and Kashmiri in this list.

name: Malay
description: Malay is an Austronesian language spoken primarily in Malaysia, Brunei, and Singapore, serving as the official language in these regions and as a lingua franca across Southeast Asia.
boundaries: Malay is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the primary language of Malaysia and the official language of the Malay Sultanates, whereas other siblings represent either geographically distinct languages, languages of different language families, or languages with different primary geographic regions of use.

name: Maltese
description: Maltese is a Semitic language spoken primarily in Malta, characterized by a unique blend of Semitic grammar with substantial Romance language vocabulary influence.
boundaries: Maltese is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of Malta and the only Semitic language among the Romance and Indo-European languages that dominate the sibling list.

name: Burmese
description: Content tagged with Burmese language is material written in or primarily presented in the Myanmar language, the official language of Myanmar (formerly Burma) and spoken by the Burmese ethnic majority.
boundaries: Burmese is distinguished from its sibling categories by its status as a Sino-Tibetan language specific to Myanmar and the Burmese people, rather than being a language of other Southeast Asian, South Asian, European, African, or other linguistic regions represented among the sibling categories.

name: Nauruan
description: Nauruan is an Austronesian language spoken as the official language of the island nation of Nauru in the central Pacific Ocean.
boundaries: Nauruan is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole language indigenous to Nauru, whereas the other siblings represent languages from diverse geographic regions and language families across Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Americas.

name: Norwegian Bokmal
description: Norwegian Bokmål is a standardized written form of Norwegian that emerged in the 19th century as a Norwegianized version of Danish-Norwegian, and is one of two official written standards of the Norwegian language.
boundaries: Norwegian Bokmål is distinguished from its sibling Norwegian Nynorsk by being the more widely used written standard based on eastern Norwegian dialects, while Nynorsk is a less common standard constructed from rural Norwegian dialects; it differs from Norwegian (which encompasses both standards) by representing specifically the Bokmål variant rather than the language as a whole.

name: Northern Ndebele
description: Content in Northern Ndebele is written in or translated into Ndebele (Sindebele), a Bantu language spoken primarily in Zimbabwe and South Africa.
boundaries: Northern Ndebele is distinguished from its sibling Southern Ndebele by geographic origin and linguistic classification, with Northern Ndebele being the language of the Ndebele people of Zimbabwe, while Southern Ndebele is spoken in South Africa.

name: Nepali
description: Nepali is an Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in Nepal and by diaspora communities, written in the Devanagari script.
boundaries: Nepali is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole representative of the Nepali language, while siblings encompass other distinct languages ranging across Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Pacific regions.

name: Ndonga
description: Ndonga is a Bantu language spoken primarily in Namibia by the Ndonga people as their native language.
boundaries: Ndonga is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a southwestern Bantu language of the Ovambo group, whereas siblings include languages from other Bantu branches, Indo-European families, Afro-Asiatic, Austronesian, Sino-Tibetan, and other language families across the world.

name: Dutch
description: Dutch is a West Germanic language spoken primarily in the Netherlands and Belgium, characterized by its grammatical structure and vocabulary derived from Germanic and Low Franconian roots.
boundaries: Dutch is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Germanic language with its own ISO 639-1 code (nl), separate from but related to languages like German, Afrikaans, and English.

name: Norwegian Nynorsk
description: Content written in Norwegian Nynorsk, one of the two official written standards of the Norwegian language, characterized by its grammar, vocabulary, and orthographic conventions.
boundaries: Norwegian Nynorsk is distinguished from Norwegian Bokmal and other Scandinavian languages by its specific standardized spelling, morphology, and lexical choices that reflect rural and western Norwegian dialects rather than the Danish-influenced urban Oslo standard.

name: Norwegian
description: Content written primarily in Norwegian, a North Germanic language spoken in Norway.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from Norwegian Bokmal and Norwegian Nynorsk by encompassing both written standards of Norwegian, while those sibling categories represent the specific standardized forms individually.

name: Southern Ndebele
description: Southern Ndebele is a Bantu language spoken primarily in South Africa by the Southern Ndebele people, characterized by its distinctive phonological features and noun class system.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from Northern Ndebele (spoken in Zimbabwe) and other Bantu languages by its specific geographic distribution in the Mpumalanga and Limpopo provinces of South Africa and its particular dialect features.

name: Navajo
description: Content primarily produced in, translated into, or specifically about the Navajo language, an Athabaskan language spoken by Navajo people in the southwestern United States.
boundaries: Navajo is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Native American language of the Athabaskan family, whereas siblings include major world languages (English, Mandarin, Spanish), European languages (French, German, Polish), African languages (Swahili, Hausa, Yoruba), and other language families and regions globally.

name: Chichewa
description: Chichewa is a Bantu language spoken primarily in Malawi and neighboring regions of Zambia and Mozambique.
boundaries: Chichewa is distinguished from its siblings as a Bantu language of Southern Africa, whereas most siblings are either non-Bantu languages, Bantu languages from other regions, or constructed/classical languages.

name: Occitan
description: Occitan is a Romance language historically spoken in southern France and parts of Spain, Italy, and Monaco, characterized by its distinctive phonology and grammatical features distinct from French and other regional Romance languages.
boundaries: Occitan is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Romance language with its own standardized orthography and literary tradition, rather than being another major European or world language, and by its geographic and linguistic position between French and Catalan.

name: Ojibwe
description: This category contains content that is written in or primarily presented in the Ojibwe language, an Anishinaupic Algonquian language spoken by Ojibwe peoples in North America.
boundaries: Ojibwe is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Native American language of the Great Lakes and northern plains regions, rather than a language of Europe, Asia, Africa, or other world regions represented among the sibling categories.

name: Oromo
description: Content written in Oromo, a Cushitic language spoken primarily in Ethiopia and Kenya.
boundaries: Oromo is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Cushitic language of the Afro-Asiatic family, whereas most siblings are from different language families (Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Niger-Congo, Austronesian, etc.) or represent other Afro-Asiatic branches like Semitic (Arabic, Hebrew, Amharic) or Berber languages.

name: Oriya
description: Content is written in or translated into Oriya (also known as Odia), a Indo-Aryan language spoken primarily in the Indian state of Odisha.
boundaries: Oriya is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as an Eastern Indo-Aryan language, separate from other Indian languages like Hindi, Bengali, Assamese, and Telugu that are represented among the siblings.

name: Ossetian
description: Content in the Ossetian language, spoken by Ossetian peoples primarily in the North Caucasus region of Russia and South Ossetia.
boundaries: Ossetian is distinguished from its siblings as an Indo-European language of the Iranian branch, whereas most siblings are from Afro-Asiatic, Sino-Tibetan, Niger-Congo, Austronesian, or other language families.

name: Punjabi
description: Content in the Punjabi language, including text, audio, and video primarily composed in Punjabi as spoken and written in Punjab and Punjabi diaspora communities.
boundaries: Punjabi is distinguished from its sibling categories as the only category representing the Indo-Aryan language historically and primarily associated with the Punjab region, using its own script systems (Gurmukhi or Shahmukhi).

name: Pali
description: Pali is an ancient Indo-Aryan language primarily used as the liturgical and scholarly language of Theravada Buddhism, in which the earliest Buddhist texts and scriptures were composed and transmitted.
