boundaries: Pali is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an extinct classical language of historical and religious significance rather than a modern living language spoken as a primary means of communication by contemporary populations.

name: Polish
description: Polish is a language primarily spoken in Poland and represents the West Slavic branch of the Indo-European language family.
boundaries: Polish is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic classification as a West Slavic language, differentiating it from other Slavic languages (such as Russian, Ukrainian, Czech, Slovak) and all non-Slavic languages in the list.

name: Pashto
description: Content in Pashto language, a member of the Indo-Iranian language family primarily spoken in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
boundaries: Pashto is distinguished from its siblings by being an Indo-Iranian language with a distinct phonological system and vocabulary, whereas sibling categories encompass languages from diverse language families including Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic, Niger-Congo, Altaic, and Germanic families.

name: Portuguese
description: Portuguese is a Romance language primarily spoken in Portugal, Brazil, Angola, and other former Portuguese colonies, characterized by its phonetic and grammatical features distinct from other Iberian languages.
boundaries: Portuguese is distinguished from its sibling categories by its unique phonological system, verb conjugation patterns, and lexical inventory, separating it from Spanish, Galician, and other Romance languages within this language taxonomy.

name: Quechua
description: Content in Quechua language is text, audio, video, or other media primarily composed in or translated into Quechua, an indigenous language family spoken in the Andes region of South America.
boundaries: Quechua is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an indigenous Amerindian language of South America, rather than a European, African, Asian, or other language family represented in the broader Content Language taxonomy.

name: Romansh
description: Content in the Romansh language, a Rhaeto-Romance language spoken primarily in the Graubünden region of southeastern Switzerland.
boundaries: Romansh is distinguished from its siblings by being a minority Romance language of Switzerland with approximately 40,000 speakers, separate from the larger Romance languages like French, Italian, Spanish, and Romanian, and from other regional European languages in this comprehensive language taxonomy.

name: Kirundi
description: Content in this category is specifically written in or presented in the Kirundi language, a Bantu language primarily spoken in Burundi and parts of Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.
boundaries: Kirundi is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the sole category designated for this particular Bantu language, while siblings represent other distinct languages from various language families across Africa, Europe, Asia, and the Pacific.

name: Romanian
description: Romanian is a Romance language spoken primarily in Romania and Moldova, characterized by Latin roots with Slavic, Greek, and Turkish influences.
boundaries: Romanian is distinguished from other Romance languages (Italian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Catalan, Sardinian, Romansh, Galician, Occitan) by its Eastern European geographic location, distinctive phonological features, and unique preservation of Latin case systems among Romance languages.

name: Russian
description: Content written or expressed primarily in the Russian language, a Slavic language spoken as a native language by Russians and as a lingua franca across much of the former Soviet Union.
boundaries: Russian is distinguished from other Slavic sibling categories (Belarusian, Bulgarian, Old Church Slavonic, Chuvash, Czech, Ukrainian, Polish, Slovak, Slovene, Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian) by its specific grammatical structures, phonology, and vocabulary, as well as from all other language categories by its use of Cyrillic script and Eastern Slavic linguistic features.

name: Kinyarwanda
description: Kinyarwanda is a Bantu language spoken primarily in Rwanda and among Rwandan diaspora communities as a first and official language.
boundaries: Kinyarwanda is distinguished from its siblings by being the primary indigenous language of Rwanda and belonging to the Bantu language family, whereas most siblings are either from different language families (Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic) or are Bantu languages of different regions (Kikuyu, Lingala, Swahili, Zulu).

name: Sanskrit
description: Sanskrit is an ancient Indo-European language of India that was the primary literary and scholarly language of classical Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain texts and continues to be used in religious and academic contexts.
boundaries: Sanskrit is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an ancient, primarily literary language of South Asian origin that belongs to the Indo-European family, whereas siblings represent either modern spoken languages, constructed languages, or languages from other geographic regions and language families.

name: Sardinian
description: Content written in Sardinian, a Romance language spoken primarily in Sardinia, Italy.
boundaries: Sardinian is distinguished from other Romance languages by its specific phonological, morphological, and lexical features characteristic of the Sardinian language, and from non-Romance languages by its classification within the Romance language family.

name: Sindhi
description: Content in Sindhi language, a language spoken primarily in the Sindh region of Pakistan and among Sindhi diaspora communities.
boundaries: Sindhi is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an Indo-Aryan language of the Sindh region, rather than languages from other geographic regions, language families, or broader linguistic groupings represented among the siblings.

name: Northern Sami
description: Northern Sami is a Uralic language spoken primarily in northern Scandinavia, particularly in northern Norway, Sweden, and Finland.
boundaries: Northern Sami is distinguished from its siblings by being a Sámi language with significant use in the Sápmi region, whereas most siblings are either major national languages, widely spoken international languages, or languages from different language families entirely.

name: Sango
description: Sango is a Ubangian language spoken primarily in the Central African Republic, serving as a lingua franca and one of the nation's official languages.
boundaries: Sango is distinguished from its siblings by being the primary language of Central Africa, whereas its sibling categories represent languages from other African regions (Swahili, Yoruba, Zulu), European regions (French, German, English), Asian regions (Japanese, Hindi, Arabic), and constructed languages (Esperanto, Interlingua).

name: Sinhala
description: Sinhala is the official language of Sri Lanka, primarily spoken by the Sinhalese people and written in the Sinhala script.
boundaries: Sinhala is distinguished from its sibling categories by being an Indo-Aryan language specific to Sri Lanka, whereas siblings include other language families (Semitic, Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic) and broader geographic distributions across Africa, Europe, Asia, and beyond.

name: Slovak
description: Slovak is a West Slavic language primarily spoken in Slovakia and serves as the official language of that country.
boundaries: Slovak is distinguished from other Slavic languages (such as Czech, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, and Slovene) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, and from non-Slavic languages by its membership in the Slavic language family.

name: Slovene
description: Slovene is a South Slavic language spoken primarily in Slovenia and by Slovenian diaspora communities worldwide.
boundaries: Slovene is distinguished from other Slavic siblings (Bulgarian, Belarusian, Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features characteristic of the South Slavic branch, and from non-Slavic siblings by its classification within the Slavic language family.

name: Samoan
description: Samoan is an Austronesian language spoken primarily in Samoa and American Samoa, with significant diaspora communities in New Zealand, Australia, and the United States.
boundaries: Samoan is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Polynesian language from the South Pacific, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Sino-Tibetan languages, or languages from African and Asian continental regions.

name: Shona
description: Content primarily composed in Shona, a Bantu language spoken mainly in Zimbabwe and parts of Mozambique and Botswana.
boundaries: Shona is distinguished from other language categories by its classification as a Bantu language of Southern Africa, separate from other African languages like Swahili, Yoruba, or Hausa, and from non-African languages in this taxonomy.

name: Somali
description: Content primarily produced in, spoken as a native language in, or linguistically belonging to the Somali language, a Cushitic language spoken in Somalia and surrounding regions.
boundaries: Somali is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Cushitic Afro-Asiatic language specific to the Horn of Africa, whereas siblings span unrelated language families across all global regions and include Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Niger-Congo, and other distinct linguistic groups.

name: Albanian
description: Content written in Albanian, the official language of Albania and a co-official language in Kosovo, North Macedonia, and Serbia.
boundaries: Albanian is distinguished from other languages by its status as the only surviving member of its own Indo-European language branch, with no particularly close relatives among the sibling categories.

name: Serbian
description: Content expressed, published, or composed in the Serbian language, a South Slavic language spoken primarily in Serbia and the region of the former Yugoslavia.
boundaries: Serbian is distinguished from other Slavic languages (Russian, Polish, Bulgarian, Croatian, Slovene, etc.) by its specific phonological, grammatical, and lexical features, and from its closest relative Croatian by standardized differences in vocabulary, pronunciation, and writing conventions.

name: Swati
description: Content expressed in Swati, a Bantu language spoken primarily in Eswatini and South Africa.
boundaries: Swati is distinguished from other languages by its specific phonological system, grammar, and vocabulary characteristic of the Swati language (ISO 639-1 code: ss), rather than other Bantu, African, or world languages in this taxonomy.

name: Southern Sotho
description: Southern Sotho is a Bantu language spoken primarily in Lesotho and South Africa, belonging to the Sotho-Tswana language group.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by representing a specific Bantu language of southern Africa, separate from other regional languages like Tswana, Xhosa, Zulu, and Swati, and from unrelated language families represented in the broader taxonomy.

name: Sundanese
description: Content that is written in or primarily uses the Sundanese language, a Western Austronesian language spoken by approximately 40 million people in West Java, Indonesia.
boundaries: Sundanese is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a specific Austronesian language of Indonesia, separate from related Indonesian languages like Javanese and from unrelated language families represented among the siblings.

name: Swedish
description: Content that is primarily written, spoken, or produced in Swedish, the North Germanic language spoken predominantly in Sweden and parts of Finland.
boundaries: Swedish is distinguished from other Scandinavian and Germanic languages (Danish, Norwegian, German, etc.) by its specific phonological features, grammar rules, and vocabulary derived from North Germanic linguistic traditions.

name: Swahili
description: Swahili is a Bantu language spoken primarily in East Africa, particularly in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, and serves as a lingua franca across the region.
boundaries: Swahili is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a major East African language with significant Bantu linguistic roots, rather than languages from other geographic regions or language families such as Indo-European, Semitic, Sino-Tibetan, or other Afro-Asiatic languages.

name: Tamil
description: Tamil is a Dravidian language primarily spoken in southern India, Sri Lanka, and by diaspora communities worldwide, used for content creation, communication, and cultural expression.
boundaries: Tamil is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a language of the Dravidian language family with its own distinct script and grammar system, separate from the Indo-European, Sino-Tibetan, Afro-Asiatic, Austronesian, and other language families represented among the siblings.

name: Telugu
description: Telugu is a Dravidian language spoken primarily in the Indian state of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, used for content creation, communication, and documentation in that language.
boundaries: Telugu is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a South Indian Dravidian language with its own distinct script and grammatical structure, separate from Indo-European languages and other language families represented among the siblings.

name: Tajik
description: Tajik is a Persian-based language spoken primarily in Tajikistan and parts of Afghanistan and Uzbekistan, written in Cyrillic script.
boundaries: Tajik differs from its sibling categories as the only Tajik-specific language option, distinct from other Persian varieties (Farsi) and Central Asian Turkic languages (Uzbek, Turkmen, Kyrgyz) also represented in this taxonomy.

name: Thai
description: Thai is a tonal language spoken primarily in Thailand, belonging to the Tai-Kadai language family and written in the Thai script.
boundaries: Thai is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of Thailand with a unique tonal system and distinct script, separate from other Southeast Asian languages like Lao, Khmer, and Vietnamese, and from all other language families represented in the sibling categories.

name: Tigrinya
description: Tigrinya is a Semitic language spoken primarily in Eritrea and the Tigray region of Ethiopia, characterized by a unique script (Ge'ez) and distinct phonological features within the Semitic language family.
boundaries: Tigrinya is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the only Semitic language from the Horn of Africa in this taxonomy that serves as an official language in Eritrea, whereas related Semitic languages like Amharic and Arabic represent different geographic and political regions.

name: Turkmen
description: Content in the Turkmen language, a Turkic language primarily spoken in Turkmenistan and by diaspora communities in Central Asia and the Middle East.
boundaries: Turkmen is distinguished from sibling categories by being a Turkic language written in the Cyrillic, Latin, or Arabic scripts, while sibling categories encompass all other world languages from various linguistic families and regions.

name: Tagalog
description: Content tagged with Tagalog language, the official language of the Philippines primarily spoken in the Manila region and used as a lingua franca across the archipelago.
boundaries: Tagalog is distinguished from other content languages by being specifically the Philippine language standardized as Filipino, rather than other Austronesian languages like Indonesian, Javanese, or Malay, or any of the non-Austronesian languages in the sibling set.

name: Tswana
description: Tswana is a Bantu language spoken primarily in Botswana and South Africa, used as both an official and community language by millions of native speakers.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by representing specifically the Tswana language, rather than other African languages like Zulu or Xhosa, or non-African languages like English or Mandarin Chinese in the broader Content Language taxonomy.

name: Tonga
description: Content in the Tonga language, which is primarily spoken in the Kingdom of Tonga and by diaspora communities in the Pacific region and beyond.
boundaries: Tonga is distinguished from its sibling language categories by being a Austronesian language specific to Tongan speakers, rather than languages from African, European, Asian, or other geographic and linguistic families represented in the siblings list.

name: Turkish
description: Turkish is a Turkic language primarily spoken in Turkey and Cyprus, characterized by agglutinative grammar and vowel harmony.
boundaries: Turkish is distinguished from its sibling categories as a Turkic language using the Latin alphabet, separate from other Turkic languages like Azerbaijani, Turkmen, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, and Uzbek, and from non-Turkic languages across other language families represented in the siblings list.

name: Tsonga
description: Tsonga is a Bantu language spoken primarily in southern Africa, particularly in Mozambique, South Africa, and Eswatini.
boundaries: Tsonga is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Bantu language of the S.50 group, whereas most siblings are either Indo-European languages, Sino-Tibetan languages, Niger-Congo languages from non-Bantu groups, or constructed/auxiliary languages.

name: Tatar
description: Content in this category consists of text, media, or resources primarily composed in or translated into Tatar, a Turkic language spoken predominantly in Russia's Tatarstan region and diaspora communities.
boundaries: Tatar is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Turkic language with Cyrillic orthography, whereas its siblings represent diverse language families including Romance, Germanic, Slavic, Semitic, Sino-Tibetan, Indo-Aryan, Afro-Asiatic, and other linguistic groups with their respective writing systems.

name: Twi
description: Content is primarily composed of text, audio, video, or multimedia materials created in or translated into the Twi language, which is a major language of the Akan group spoken primarily in Ghana.
boundaries: Twi is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as an Akan language with distinct phonology, grammar, and orthography, separate from other African, European, Asian, and constructed languages in the broader Content Language taxonomy.

name: Tahitian
description: Content written or produced in the Tahitian language, the Austronesian language native to Tahiti and other islands in French Polynesia.
boundaries: Tahitian is distinguished from its sibling categories by being a Polynesian language spoken in the South Pacific, whereas siblings are languages from other geographic regions and language families such as African, European, Asian, or constructed languages.

name: Uyghur
description: This category contains content written in Uyghur, a Turkic language primarily spoken in the Xinjiang region of China and diaspora communities.
boundaries: Uyghur is distinguished from its sibling language categories by being a Turkic language with its own distinct phonology, grammar, and script tradition (historically Arabic script, currently Cyrillic and Latin variants), rather than belonging to other language families represented in the sibling list such as Sino-Tibetan, Indo-European, Afro-Asiatic, or Niger-Congo families.

name: Ukrainian
description: Ukrainian is a content category for textual, audiovisual, or multimedia resources produced in or translated into the Ukrainian language, which is the official language of Ukraine and belongs to the East Slavic language family.
boundaries: Ukrainian is distinguished from its sibling categories by its specific linguistic identity as an East Slavic language, separate from other Slavic languages like Russian, Polish, Bulgarian, and Czech, and from all non-Slavic languages in the broader language taxonomy.

name: Urdu
description: Urdu is an Indo-Aryan language primarily spoken in Pakistan and parts of India, characterized by Persian and Arabic influences in its vocabulary and written in the Perso-Arabic script.
boundaries: Urdu is distinguished from its sibling categories by being the official language of Pakistan and a scheduled language of India, rather than being the primary or official language of other nations or regions represented in the sibling set.

name: Uzbek
description: Content written in or translated into Uzbek, a Turkic language spoken primarily in Uzbekistan and surrounding regions.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from sibling language categories by specifically identifying Uzbek as the language of the content, rather than any other of the 200+ languages represented in the Content Language taxonomy.

name: Venda
description: Content that is written in Venda, a Bantu language primarily spoken in the Limpopo province of South Africa and parts of Zimbabwe.
boundaries: Venda is distinguished from other sibling language categories by being a Bantu language of southern Africa, separate from other African languages like Swahili, Yoruba, and Igbo, and from non-African languages in the sibling set.

name: Vietnamese
description: Vietnamese is a tonal, monosyllabic language spoken primarily in Vietnam and by diaspora communities, written in the Latin script with diacritical marks.
boundaries: Vietnamese is distinguished from its siblings by being the primary language of Vietnam, characterized by its tonal phonology and use of the Latin alphabet rather than logographic or other script systems used by geographically or linguistically related languages.

name: Volapuk
description: Volapük is a constructed international auxiliary language created in 1879 by Johann Martin Schleyer, designed to be easy to learn and promote peace through universal communication.
boundaries: Volapük differs from its sibling categories as the only completely artificial, systematically invented language, whereas all siblings are natural languages that evolved organically within human communities.

name: Walloon
description: Content in Walloon consists of text, media, or other materials created in or translated into Walloon, a Romance language spoken primarily in the Wallonia region of Belgium.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by encompassing only resources in Walloon rather than other individual languages like French, Dutch, German, or other Romance and non-Romance languages listed.

name: Wolof
description: Wolof is a Niger-Congo language spoken primarily in Senegal and Gambia, belonging to the Senegambian branch of the Atlantic language family.
boundaries: Wolof is distinguished from its sibling categories as the sole representative of the Senegambian language group, whereas siblings represent other distinct languages from diverse families across Africa, Europe, Asia, and beyond.

name: Yemen
description: Content that originates from or is primarily associated with Yemen, a country located on the Arabian Peninsula in Western Asia.
boundaries: Yemen is distinguished from its sibling country categories by its specific geographic location and political sovereignty as an independent nation-state, rather than being a region, territory, or dependency of another country.

name: Zambia
description: Content originating from or produced within the geographical boundaries of the Republic of Zambia, a Southern African nation.
boundaries: Zambia is distinguished from all other country categories by its specific sovereign territory, borders, and political jurisdiction in south-central Africa between Tanzania and Zimbabwe.

name: Zimbabwe
description: Content from sources physically located in or originating from Zimbabwe, a landlocked country in southern Africa bordered by Zambia, Botswana, South Africa, and Mozambique.
boundaries: Zimbabwe is distinguished from its sibling countries by its specific geographic location in south-central Africa, distinct from neighboring nations like Zambia, Botswana, South Africa, and Mozambique, as well as all other sovereign states and territories worldwide.

name: Region/State
description: Content that originates from or is primarily associated with a specific state, province, or other first-level administrative subdivision within a country.
boundaries: This category captures regional-level geographic origin more granular than country-level but broader than metropolitan or city-level sources, distinguishing it from its siblings by focusing on the primary administrative division below the national level.

name: Metro
description: Metropolitan areas and multi-city urban conglomerations that function as integrated economic and cultural zones, typically spanning multiple jurisdictions.
boundaries: Metro is distinguished from City by encompassing entire urban agglomerations rather than single municipal boundaries, from Region/State by being sub-regional urban clusters, from Country by being sub-national, and from Continent by being highly localized geographic zones.

name: City
description: Cities are the smallest geographic units used to classify content sources, representing specific municipal areas or urban centers with defined administrative boundaries.
boundaries: This category is distinguished from its siblings by capturing content originating from individual cities rather than larger continental, country, or region-level areas, and from Metro by focusing on the city proper rather than its broader metropolitan area.
